payload.friendly_name: Pack doctrine artefacts: directive, styleguide, paradigm
payload.purpose_context: The charter service models only the tactic artefact as a rich pack entity today; the other doctrine artefacts are read as generic facts. This mission gives the three prose doctrine artefacts (directive, styleguide, paradigm) the same first-class treatment as the tactic — typed identity, invariants, storage round-trip and repository access — so the service can read and write them faithfully, continuing the packs slice without touching the harder asset, profile and mission-type tiers.
payload.purpose_tldr: Model the directive, styleguide and paradigm charter artefacts as first-class pack entities that survive a YAML round trip.

options: Per-kind entities (3 classes, each like Tactic)
Generic DoctrineArtifact with a kind discriminator
payload.question: Model directive/styleguide/paradigm as per-kind entities (each like Tactic) or one generic DoctrineArtifact child entity with a kind discriminator — and does the existing bespoke Tactic fold in or stay special?

payload.final_answer: Per-kind concrete child entities (Directive, Styleguide, Paradigm) each modelled like Tactic and carrying its own schema-distinct body, unified by a thin CharterArtifact interface in kernel.domain — NOT one generic DoctrineArtifact. CharterArtifact spine: kind(), packId(), localId(), schemaVersion(), label() (title|name), description() (Optional: intent|summary|purpose), edges() (references/procedures/directive_refs -> DRG edges), default urn(). Tactic is retrofitted to implement CharterArtifact and stays special (keeps steps/failureModes). 'doctrine' is not canonical; family + interface are named CharterArtifact and code uses American 'artifact'.
payload.rationale: Operator rejected over-generalizing into one class after we confirmed against the canonical per-kind schemas (ADR-0017 / open-packs) that directive (intent+enforcement+integrity/validation rules), styleguide (scope+principles+patterns+structural_lint_config) and paradigm (summary+directive_refs) share almost no fields beyond id/schema_version/references — even the human label splits title vs name. A shared interface captures the real common spine for aggregate/repository/DRG/round-trip binding without collapsing distinct concepts.
